preamble: Devoicing of the voiced alveolar sibilant [z] to [s]. In Chinese, the Middle Chinese voiced fricative initial 邪 *z- devoiced to s- in Mandarin; the former voicing survives only as a tonal register difference. In Spanish, the Old Spanish voiced apico-alveolar /z̺/, spelled with a single intervocalic s as in casa, lost its voicing in the 16th century and merged with /s̺/, while Portuguese kept the contrast. In Russian, word-final /z/ is devoiced to [s], so глаз 'eye' is pronounced [ɡlas] while the voiced consonant returns before a vowel in the genitive глаза.

examples.from: Middle Chinese 寺 ziH (邪 initial) 'temple'
examples.note: The voiced initial z- devoiced to s-. The departing-tone syllable joins the Mandarin falling tone, as all departing-tone syllables do.

examples.from: Middle Chinese 俗 zjowk (邪 initial, entering tone) 'custom, vulgar'
examples.note: The voiced initial z- devoiced to s-, and the syllable now carries the yang-register rising tone (yangping).

examples.from: Middle Chinese 隨 zjwe (邪 initial) 'follow'
examples.note: The voiced initial z- devoiced to s-, and the level-tone syllable carries the yang-register rising tone (yangping).
In the 16th century the three voiced sibilants lost their voicing and merged with the voiceless ones; the apico-alveolar /z̺/ became /s̺/. Portuguese casa [ˈkazɐ] keeps the older voiced sibilant.
Same 16th-century devoicing of intervocalic /z̺/; Portuguese coisa keeps [z].
Word-final devoicing of /z/ to [s]; a positional neutralization, so the voiced variant surfaces before vowels.

examples.note: Word-final *z was devoiced to s in Gothic, while North and West Germanic turned it into r or lost it (Old Norse dagr, fiskr).
